description: Fix globe marker rendering by switching from r3f-globe to react-globe.gl which manages CSS2DRenderer automatically

userStories.title: Install react-globe.gl
userStories.description: As a developer, I need react-globe.gl installed so the globe component can use its built-in CSS2DRenderer for HTML marker rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: Run: npm install react-globe.gl
react-globe.gl is installed successfully
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
Do NOT uninstall r3f-globe or @react-three/fiber or @react-three/drei yet
userStories.notes: react-globe.gl wraps the same three-globe core as r3f-globe but manages the full rendering pipeline including CSS2DRenderer

userStories.title: Rewrite photo-globe.tsx to use react-globe.gl Globe component
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to replace the R3F Canvas + r3f-globe setup with react-globe.gl's standalone Globe component which handles WebGLRenderer + CSS2DRenderer internally.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace R3F imports (Canvas from @react-three/fiber, OrbitControls from @react-three/drei, R3fGlobe from r3f-globe, OrbitControlsImpl from three-stdlib) with: import Globe from 'react-globe.gl' (default import)
Do NOT wrap Globe in <Canvas> — react-globe.gl creates its own canvas internally
Remove <ambientLight>, <directionalLight>, <OrbitControls> — react-globe.gl manages these
Use useRef<any>(null) for the Globe ref (globeEl)
Set Globe props: globeImageUrl, bumpImageUrl, showAtmosphere={true}, atmosphereColor='lightskyblue', atmosphereAltitude={0.2}, backgroundColor='#0a0a0a'
For sizing: measure the container div using a ref and ResizeObserver, pass width and height as number props to Globe. Or use the window inner dimensions minus nav height (56px)
After globe mounts (useEffect with globeEl.current check): set globeEl.current.controls().autoRotate = true, autoRotateSpeed = 0.5, enablePan = false, minDistance = 120, maxDistance = 800
Auto-rotation pause on interaction: globeEl.current.controls().addEventListener('start', ...) to set autoRotate=false, addEventListener('end', ...) to resume after 3s idle setTimeout
Set initial point of view: globeEl.current.pointOfView({ altitude: 2.5 }) after mount
Keep globe fade-in: opacity 0→1 container div with onGlobeReady callback setting state to true
Keep empty state: if (!loading && points.length === 0) return 'No photos with location data yet' message
CRITICAL: All hooks (useState, useRef, useCallback, useMemo, useEffect) must be declared BEFORE any early return statement
The parent page src/app/(dashboard)/map/page.tsx already uses next/dynamic with { ssr: false } — verify it still imports correctly
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: react-globe.gl is NOT an R3F component. It manages its own Three.js scene and renderers. Do NOT use <Canvas>. Access controls via ref: globeEl.current.controls(). The Globe component renders a canvas element directly.

userStories.title: Wire up HTML markers with htmlElementsData
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my photo thumbnails on the globe at their GPS coordinates, rendered as interactive HTML elements using react-globe.gl's built-in CSS2DRenderer.
acceptanceCriteria: Pass htmlElementsData={clusterData} to Globe component (same ClusterMarkerData[] state as before)
Pass htmlLat='lat' and htmlLng='lng' string accessors
Pass htmlAltitude={0.01}
Pass htmlElement accessor: (d) => createMarkerElement(d as ClusterMarkerData, handleNavigate) — reuse existing create-marker-element.ts
Pass htmlTransitionDuration={500}
Keep the existing useEffect that fetches thumbnail URLs via useUrlCache and builds clusterData from clusters
Keep useGeoMedia() hook for fetching geo points
Keep clusterPoints() from geo-utils.ts for clustering
CRITICAL: Markers must be VISIBLE on the globe — this is the whole point of switching to react-globe.gl
Clicking a single marker navigates to /groups/{groupId}
Hovering a cluster fans out thumbnails, clicking navigates to group
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill — markers must be visible on the globe
userStories.notes: react-globe.gl automatically sets up CSS2DRenderer, which is why HTML markers will now render. The htmlElement prop signature is identical: (d: object) => HTMLElement. The existing createMarkerElement function should work as-is.

userStories.title: Wire up labels and verify full functionality
userStories.description: As a user, I want location labels near photo clusters and full interactive globe functionality.
acceptanceCriteria: Pass labelsData, labelLat='lat', labelLng='lng', labelText='text' to Globe
labelSize={0.4}, labelAltitude={0.015}, labelDotRadius={0}
labelsTransitionDuration={500}
Auto-rotation works: globe slowly spins when idle
Auto-rotation pauses on user drag/zoom, resumes after 3 seconds
Pan is disabled (enablePan = false on controls)
Globe has atmospheric glow effect
Globe fades in on initial load
Empty state shows when no geo-tagged photos exist
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: react-globe.gl supports the same label props as r3f-globe since they share the three-globe core. labelIncludeDot may or may not be supported — if not, just use labelDotRadius={0}.
